evidence: All three scored dimensions carry explicit independence-and-continue wording, and none tells the judge to stop at a first failure. functional/prompt.md:53-55 'Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion.' Also :9 'that criterion fails and scores 0; report what you saw and move on to the next criterion', :29 'Two failed attempts at the same control fail that criterion; continue.', and :24-25 'Never carry a verdict across criteria'. polish/prompt.md:20-26 '## Independent scoring ... One failed criterion does not zero the others. If a criterion cannot be performed, mark it failed and continue to every remaining criterion; return a verdict for all of them. The global browser gate is the only all-or-nothing rule'. visual/prompt.md:38-43 has the same block, using the 0 anchor for criteria that cannot be performed. This wording matches or adds to the frozen template (template functional :68-69, polish :14-20, visual :44-49). The only all-or-nothing rule is the in-dimension global browser gate (functional :11-19, polish :10-18, visual :18-26), which is template policy, not a per-criterion cascade. Structure reinforces this: functional judge.toml:6 uses mode = "individual" (one session per criterion, so one criterion's failure or timeout cannot end the others), and polish/visual are batched with the wording above. Gates render and constraints use aggregation = "all_pass" and are exempt. Grep for stop/abort/halt/zero across scored prompts, app_context.md and judge.toml found no stop-on-first-failure instruction. app_context.md (28 lines) contains none of these terms. I tried two counterexamples. (a) A broken app that fails an early functional criterion, such as wall_every_route, still gets separate verdicts for the later criteria because each runs in its own session, and every criterion builds its own positive controls (for example JUDGE-CS1, JUDGE-W0 and JUDGE-H3). The independence wording does not let a broken app pass anything. (b) A conforming app that is penalized because the judge stops after a sibling's miss is excluded by the wording in all three prompts. Residual observations, none a row-38 defect: (1) functional :45-46 says 'Every refusal pairs with a success of the same kind ... in the same criterion or an earlier one'. In individual mode an earlier session's evidence is not visible, but each criterion supplies its own positive control, so this creates no zero-cascade. Its feasibility belongs to rows 28/37. (2) In functional :54-55 the phrase 'after any / failure' wraps across a line, whereas the template keeps 'any failure' on one line. 'Score each criterion independently' is on a single line, so a line-based checker would still find it, but the private checker executable was not run. Run evidence: no configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: scripted golden only), so judge compliance with the wording is not measured. This row is a source-wording check and needs no runtime measurement.
